characters.name: [Full name]
characters.physical_description: [Appearance and bearing. What a stranger registers first. Specific enough to be a writing tool. 2-4 sentences.]
characters.personality: [Who they are: temperament, social intelligence, wounds, humor, what makes them dangerous or compelling. 3-5 sentences.]
characters.dialogue_style: [First person [tense]. How they sound: register, wit level, what they reach for under pressure, what they refuse to say directly. 2-4 sentences.]
characters.backstory: [What happened before page one that shapes every choice they make. 3-5 sentences.]
characters.want: [What they consciously pursue — specific and external]
characters.need: [What they actually lack — often the opposite of their armor]
characters.flaw: [The specific way their armor costs them things they want]
characters.chemistry_with_protagonist: [What the other protagonist does that gets through. What they find impossible to dismiss. 3-5 sentences.]
characters.romantic_obstacles: [What stands between them — structural, informational, emotional. Specific conditions that must change for the story to resolve. 2-4 sentences.]
characters.shared_history: [What they have before the story starts, or what is built in the first act that makes everything after feel inevitable]
characters.internal_monologue: [How their POV voice sounds: what it notices first, what it jokes about, what it goes quiet about, where sensation lives before the mind catches up. This is a writing instruction. 4-6 sentences.]
characters.relationship_dynamics: [Per named relationship: how they read this person, what they want from them, what they won't say. 1-3 sentences per relationship.]

characters.name: [Full name]
characters.physical_description: [Appearance and bearing. How they carry power.]
characters.dialogue_style: [Register and style — how they sound, what they never say directly]
characters.motivations: [What they actually want and why it makes sense to them. Not just evil — specific and coherent. 2-3 sentences.]
characters.methods: [How they operate: the specific tools, the administrative calm, what they use as leverage]
characters.power_resources: [What they control: money, information, relationships, mutual embarrassment, access]
characters.relationship_to_protagonist: [How they relate to each protagonist and what each one represents in their plans. 2-3 sentences.]

characters.name: [Full name]
characters.physical_description: [1-2 sentences: the physical fact the writer needs]
characters.personality: [Who they are in the story's world — 2-3 sentences]
characters.skills_or_resources: [What they bring: access, information, money, social capital]
characters.role_in_story: [Narrative function: what they enable, block, or reveal. What the story cannot do without them.]
characters.relationship_to_protagonist: [How they relate to the protagonists — what they see, what they offer, what they miss]
